title: Learning: Short Lives
text: Billing's identity is about to expire. Later, the ledger receives a call from a certificate that was withdrawn this morning.
held: The key never left the workload, and renewal happened before anything broke.

cards.label: Renew now and swap certificates without dropping calls
Keep using the old one until something breaks
cards.why: Something breaking is the outage. Renewal is routine precisely so that expiry never arrives as a surprise.

temptations.label: Copy the private key to a shared volume so every replica can use it
temptations.why: A key on a shared volume belongs to everything that can mount the volume. Each replica gets its own identity; keys don't travel.

cards.label: Refuse the request
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: status
fields.check: Check the certificate against the revocation list

intrusion.value: withdrawn this morning: its key was exposed
intrusion.detail: This certificate was revoked this morning after its key was exposed.
intrusion.why: A revoked certificate still looks valid until someone checks the list. That check is the only thing revocation does.
intrusion.reveal: The certificate presented had been revoked that morning after its key was exposed.

teaches: Short lifetimes turn a stolen key into a short problem.
Private keys stay inside the workload that owns them. Sharing one makes several things indistinguishable.
Revocation works only for receivers that look.
